reviews.one_line_contribution: Using ALFWorld's type/instance structure to split the privileged context of a memory-conditioned self-teacher into a type-level procedure share (same-type walkthroughs from other floorplans) and an instance-bound share (the game's own walkthrough), and testing the claim that only the type share distils into a memory-free student while the instance share reappears, objective-invariantly, as the student's privileged-vs-unprivileged deployment gap.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified: UCOB (arXiv:2606.29502, verified via s2cli search and paper lookup, 8 citations) is the closest agent-side threat — it already treats retrieved skill memory as a privileged teacher prompt on ALFWorld/WebShop and its abstract explicitly attacks the privileged-teacher assumption ('retrieved skills are not oracular: they may help in one state while misleading the same policy in another'), i.e. it already problematizes the same illusion with agent memory. It does not, however, decompose the privileged information into instance- vs type-level shares, does not run token-matched decoy/empty conditions, and reports performance rather than a memory-free deployment gap, so it does not scoop the decomposition. Second: OP²SD (2608.09228, verified) performs the same logical move on math — substituting unrelated problem-solution pairs to show the gain is context-induced rather than reference-attributable; the proposal's contribution over it is the intermediate TYP cell (same type, other instance), which is the genuinely new condition. Also verified as adjacent but non-colliding: LOPSD 2608.13040 (learns privileged teaching context end-to-end), SMRC-SD 2608.05219, DAPD 2608.01735, DOPD 2606.30626, Skill-SD 2604.10674, SKILL0 2604.02268, Experience Distillation 2607.21051 ('Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience'), OVCSD 2607.27937, 2608.25936. CardDistill/SkillLens 2608.10775, which the proposal names as one of its two 'closest collisions', could NOT be verified — `paper 2608.10775` returned 'not found on S2 or HF' and a targeted keyword search for SkillLens/CardDistill/state-conditioned memory cards returned nothing matching (it surfaced FocusMem 2608.04530 and GUI-SD 2605.00642 instead). I treat that citation as unverified and possibly non-existent.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central prediction P2 is close to definitional, which the brief itself forbids ('No prediction entailed by a definition'). The ORC teacher is conditioned on the walkthrough of a TRAINING task in pool T; evaluation is on valid_seen/valid_unseen/H, whose own walkthroughs are never available at training. Instance-bound information about an evaluation game therefore cannot be in the weights by construction — no objective can encode where the pepper shaker sits in a game that was never trained on and whose object placements are re-sampled. So 'the instance share does not distil' is guaranteed by the partition, not discovered, and the only non-trivial content is the second-order scene-prior ablation. A second, independent and more damaging version of the objection runs the other way for the CD arm: the ORC teacher will succeed far more often than the TYP teacher, so CD-ORC is trained on more and cleaner successful rollouts than CD-TYP. The plan matches examples only for the raw-SFT arm; it never states that the CD (or OPD) arms are matched on number/quality of distillation trajectories. If CD-ORC beats CD-TYP memory-free, the paper cannot tell 'instance bindings distil' from 'the oracle teacher simply produced better training data'. Third, P4 is underpowered by the proposal's own noise arithmetic: it states ±6 net for a difference of differences, while its equivalence window is [0.7,1.3]×instance share, i.e. ±0.3×8 = ±2.4 net at the Gate-0 minimum — the objective-invariance claim cannot be resolved unless the instance share turns out to be ~20 net. And P2's own falsifier (0.5×instance share ≈ 4 net) sits exactly at the stated ±4 single-contrast MDE, so a 'confirmed' P2 will often be a failure to reject.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Break the definitional entailment by adding an in-distribution instance arm: distil an ORC teacher on a set of games that ARE in the evaluation set (or evaluate a subset of T with its own walkthroughs as the oracle at train time), so there is a regime in which instance-bound information could in principle be encoded. That arm is simultaneously the positive control the brief demands before asserting a 'does not transfer' null: show the pipeline CAN encode instance bindings when they are in-distribution, then show it does not when they are not. (2) Match the distillation corpora across teacher conditions — same number of successful trajectories, same token count, ideally same set of tasks — or report the retained fraction per unit of successful supervision, so P2 and P3 are not confounded with teacher success rate. (3) Re-power P4 or demote it: either raise the confirmatory seeds until the DiD CI is below the equivalence window implied by the realised Gate-0 instance share, or pre-register P4 as exploratory and make P3+P5 (retained type share and the procedure-held-out type) the confirmatory core. (4) Drop or verify 2608.10775; re-run the collision check with the intermediate-condition framing ('same-task-type versus same-instance privileged context') rather than only method names. (5) Reconcile the budget with the arm count (see missing_baseline / feasibility note): 17+ students × 698 games × 4 test blocks × 2 seeds is ~95k episodes, not the ~18k stated.
reviews.missing_baseline: An in-distribution instance-information positive control — a teacher/student arm in which the oracle walkthrough of an EVALUATION game is present at training time (e.g. distil on a slice of games that are then re-evaluated), which is the only arm that can separate 'the instance share does not distil under any objective' from 'the instance share was never in the training distribution'. Secondary omission: an example-matched CD control (teacher rollouts subsampled so that CD-ORC and CD-TYP train on the same number of successful trajectories), without which the ORC-vs-TYP contrast is confounded with teacher success rate. Also absent: UCOB (2606.29502), the published agent-side objective the brief names as a required reimplemented baseline for this exact question, appears nowhere in the arm list even though it is the closest verified prior method.

Verification of IDs the novelty argument rests on: VERIFIED — 2608.09228 (OP²SD), 2608.01735 (DAPD), 2606.30626 (DOPD), 2608.25936 (critical review), 2608.05219 (SMRC-SD, confirmed by `paper`), 2608.13040 (LOPSD), 2607.21051 (Experience Distillation, actual title 'Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience'), 2607.27937 (OVCSD), 2606.29502 (UCOB), 2608.12218. NOT VERIFIED — 2608.10775 (CardDistill/SkillLens): `paper 2608.10775` returned 'not found on S2 or HF' and a targeted search found no such work. That ID is named in the Related Work AND as one of the two 'closest collisions' in the proposal's own check, so the check's headline conclusion rests partly on a citation I could not confirm exists. Otherwise the check itself is above average for this round: three real queries, --recent used, channel status reported, and its returned IDs reproduce on my re-runs. Its weakness is framing, not effort — every query was method-named ('context distillation', 'privileged teacher'), none searched the actual novel object (an instance-vs-type decomposition of a retrieval gain), which is why it cannot claim the decomposition is unclaimed with much force; my Q2/Q4/Q6 fill that hole and also returned empty, which I report as empty.
